subject: Hosted inference queueing incident — customer notification & next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Adam Cole <adam.cole@brightpath.ai>, sre@brightpath.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted inference queueing incident — short notice

Hi Adam / BrightPath oncall team,

We're reporting an active service impact on the Redwood Hosted API that may affect some inference requests for your production routes (especially short-prefix, high-concurrency patterns). We observed sustained queue growth on the hosted inference pool in us-west starting ~08:40 UTC. Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 response times and intermittent 503s for a subset of requests.

What we are doing now: we have an active SRE bridge, performing targeted routing to alternate capacity and a rolling remediation to clear stuck queues. We will provide regular updates on the public status page and here.

Immediate ask: could you confirm whether BrightPath is seeing user-facing errors or increased client-side retries? Any short samples of failing request IDs (request-id header) would help our triage.

Status page: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/INC-2026-08-02-queueing

Apologies for the disruption — I will send an update within 30 minutes or as soon as we have mitigation.

- Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_summary.pdf (one-page live status snapshot)

From: Adam Cole <adam.cole@brightpath.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: sre@brightpath.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted inference queueing incident — short notice

Thanks Mina — we started seeing ~10% of our inference calls return 503s and spikes in latency around 09:10 PDT. Users in our dashboard show elevated error rates.

We can pull request-ids; attaching a few in the next message. For context: BrightPath has a steady stream of short-context predictions (max tokens 32) at ~800 rps to your hosted endpoint. Please advise whether you will route our traffic to a different pool or if we should throttle client-side.

Adam
Adam Cole
Head of ML Engineering, BrightPath Analytics
adam.cole@brightpath.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Adam Cole <adam.cole@brightpath.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted inference queueing incident — short notice

Mina / Lauren — quick tech summary for the thread:
- Root cause (working hypothesis): a scheduler bug combined with a rare kernel affinity edge on a subset of our us-west GPU hosts caused continuous queued work to pile up instead of being dispatched to the kernel fast path.
- Impact window: ~08:40 UTC -> mitigation in progress.
- Actions taken: (1) isolated the affected hosts, (2) kicked an automated routing policy to drain traffic to warm spare pools, (3) rolling reboot of 6 hosts to flush kernel affinity state.
- Customer-facing mitigation ETA: 15–25 minutes for majority of traffic; small fraction may see residual retries up to ~60 minutes while caches warm.

I've uploaded a set of sampled logs and request-ids to our internal bridge and am attaching a tar of request samples for BrightPath to review.

Attachment: request_sample_logs.tar.gz
Bridge / JIRA: RED-7891

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Adam Cole <adam.cole@brightpath.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted inference queueing incident — short notice

Adam — quick update:

We have diverted most BrightPath traffic away from the affected hosts and are seeing p95/p99 values trending back toward normal for your routes. We rolled a targeted remediation and are monitoring. Expected full resolution: within 30–45 minutes.

If you can, please hold off on wide client-side throttling for the next 45 minutes — the routing action should reduce user-facing errors. If your dashboard still shows elevated errors after 10 minutes, please reply with a couple of request-ids and we will prioritize them.

Status page detail: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/INC-2026-08-02-queueing

We'll follow up with a concise post-incident summary and a scheduled technical review.

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for the request samples.

— Mina

Cc: sre@brightpath.ai

Two questions: 1) will BrightPath get a post-incident report (root cause and preventative actions)? 2) did any requests fail in a way that could have caused data loss (we're concerned about incomplete streaming sessions / truncated outputs)?

Adam

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Adam Cole <adam.cole@brightpath.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: INC-2026-08-02 queueing incident

Adam — thanks again for your patience. Sharing a brief follow-up and next steps: 

1) Post-incident report: we published a short postmortem with timeline, root cause analysis, and actions: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/postmortems/INC-2026-08-02-queueing

2) Root cause (summary): an infrequent scheduler-to-kernel affinity state that prevented timely dispatch of queued inference work on an affected GPU host subset. This was triggered by a recent low-level scheduler change that regressed under a particular short-context, high-concurrency pattern.

3) Customer impact: BrightPath saw ~10% of calls return 503s and elevated p99 for ~50 minutes (start 08:40 UTC, main mitigation 09:30 UTC). No evidence of data loss; streaming sessions that observed 503s were not persisted client-side by our system and can be retried safely. We will provide a list of request-ids we observed fail if you want them for auditing.

4) Fixes and mitigations: rollback of the scheduler change, a hotfix to clear kernel affinity state on affected hosts, and an automated detection rule added to the runtime to alert earlier on queue growth patterns. We have also increased warm spare capacity for short-context workloads while the change is monitored.

5) Customer options and remediation offer: we offered BrightPath a service credit for the window of impact; if you'd like an expanded technical review call, Lauren (product ops) and Rishi (SRE) are available this week.

6) Attachments & evidence: incident_summary.pdf, request_sample_logs.tar.gz (attached).

Please let me know whether you'd like the request-id list, or to schedule the review call (we have availability Wednesday 10–12 PDT and Thursday 14–16 PDT).

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
